parameterized_queries_used.title: Parameterized Queries Used
parameterized_queries_used.description: Interpreted boolean (true = secure): all data-access queries use bound parameters / prepared statements (e.g. $1, ?, named params) rather than string-concatenated SQL built from untrusted request input. Verified via code review / SAST per OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet. False = the app concatenates user input into SQL, the primary SQL-injection enabler, so the exposure fires.

dynamic_sql_avoided.title: Dynamic SQL on Untrusted Input Avoided
dynamic_sql_avoided.description: Interpreted boolean (true = secure): the application and stored procedures avoid dynamic SQL execution on untrusted strings (no EXECUTE/EXECUTE IMMEDIATE on request-derived text) — the residual SQLi surface that survives even where most queries are parameterized. False = dynamic string-built SQL is present, so the exposure fires.

app_role_not_superuser_or_ddl.title: App DB Role Not Superuser / No DDL
app_role_not_superuser_or_ddl.description: Interpreted boolean (true = secure): the application's DB login holds only table-scoped DML (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) on its own schema and is NOT a superuser/SUPER and holds no DDL/DROP/GRANT/ALL. False = the app runs as superuser or holds DDL, so a successful injection escalates to schema tampering, COPY-to/from-program RCE (cf. CVE-2025-1094), and full takeover — the exposure fires.

strong_db_auth_method_enforced.title: Strong DB Authentication Method Enforced
strong_db_auth_method_enforced.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true only when client authentication uses a strong challenge-response method everywhere — PostgreSQL pg_hba.conf rows use scram-sha-256 (never 'trust', 'md5', or 'password' for remote hosts) and password_encryption=scram-sha-256, and MySQL/MariaDB accounts use caching_sha2_password (not the deprecated mysql_native_password). Fires (insecure) when trust/md5/password or mysql_native_password authentication is in use.

no_blank_or_default_db_passwords.title: No Blank or Default DB Passwords
no_blank_or_default_db_passwords.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when no account holds a blank/empty verifier or a default/well-known password — PostgreSQL superuser (postgres) and MySQL root set to strong non-default secrets, and no MySQL account with empty authentication_string. Fires (insecure) when any account has a blank or default/well-known password enabling default-credential login.

anonymous_db_accounts_removed.title: Anonymous DB Accounts Removed
anonymous_db_accounts_removed.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when no anonymous account exists — MySQL/MariaDB has no '' (empty user) account (verified against mysql.user where user='') and PostgreSQL has no equivalently unauthenticated catch-all login. Fires (insecure) when an anonymous '' user is present, allowing unauthenticated connection to the database.

default_accounts_removed_or_changed.title: Default Accounts Removed or Changed
default_accounts_removed_or_changed.description: Canonical cross-component interpreted-secure boolean: true when shipped/default administrative accounts have been removed or had their credentials changed from vendor defaults and remote login to default admin roles (postgres, root) is restricted. Fires (insecure) when a default account retains its shipped credential or is reachable for default-credential login.

least_privilege_access_enforced.title: Least-Privilege Access Enforced
least_privilege_access_enforced.description: Canonical attestation that the application's database principal operates under least privilege — it is NOT a superuser/owner (PostgreSQL rolsuper/rolcreatedb/rolcreaterole all false; MySQL no SUPER/ALL/WITH GRANT OPTION) and holds only the minimum privileges needed. False fires this exposure because a compromised app session or SQL injection can escalate to schema tampering, COPY-to/from-program RCE, and full data exfiltration.

role_grants_least_privilege.title: Role Grants Least Privilege
role_grants_least_privilege.description: Attestation that the application DB role holds only table-scoped DML grants (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) on its own schema and NOT DDL/DROP/GRANT/ALL or broad cross-database privileges — i.e. per-role GRANT least-privilege is in place rather than the role connecting as superuser/owner. False fires this exposure.

public_schema_create_revoked.title: PUBLIC Schema CREATE Revoked
public_schema_create_revoked.description: Attestation that the implicit PUBLIC role no longer holds CREATE on the public schema (REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC), so untrusted/low-privilege accounts cannot plant objects in the shared schema. PG15+ revokes by default but must be verified; pre-15 requires explicit REVOKE. False fires this exposure.

row_level_security_enforced_where_multit.title: Row-Level Security Enforced Where Multi-Tenant
row_level_security_enforced_where_multit.description: Attestation that, where the store holds multi-tenant or per-record-sensitive data, Row-Level Security is enabled (and FORCEd to bind table owners) with policies constraining which rows a role can see/modify — so a compromised app session cannot read other tenants' data. Vacuously true when the store is not multi-tenant. False fires this exposure.

db_not_publicly_accessible.title: DB Not Publicly Accessible
db_not_publicly_accessible.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: the database instance has NO public endpoint — RDS/Aurora/Cloud SQL/Azure SQL PubliclyAccessible=false and the instance sits in a private subnet with no internet-resolvable IP. Fires this exposure when the managed instance is publicly accessible from the internet.

listen_addresses_restricted.title: Listen Addresses Restricted
listen_addresses_restricted.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: the engine binds only to loopback or a specific private/VPC interface, never to all interfaces — PostgreSQL listen_addresses is localhost/a private IP (not '*') and MySQL/MariaDB bind_address is 127.0.0.1/a private IP (not 0.0.0.0 or ::). Fires this exposure when the DB listens on all interfaces on an internet-reachable host.

host_access_rules_scoped.title: Host Access Rules Scoped
host_access_rules_scoped.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: client host-based access rules are scoped to known private CIDRs and never permit the world — PostgreSQL pg_hba.conf host/hostssl rows do NOT use 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, and MySQL account host specifiers are not '%' for remote logins. Fires this exposure when host rules allow 0.0.0.0/0.

network_firewall_restricts_db_port.title: Network Firewall Restricts DB Port
network_firewall_restricts_db_port.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: a network firewall / security group / NACL restricts ingress to the DB port (5432/3306) to the application tier or known private ranges only, with no 0.0.0.0/0 allow on the DB port. Fires this exposure when the DB sits on a public subnet with no firewall scoping the port.

tls_only_transport.title: TLS-Only Transport Enforced
tls_only_transport.description: Server enforces TLS for all client connections so plaintext is rejected — PostgreSQL ssl=on (with pg_hba hostssl) or MySQL require_secure_transport=ON. When false, the database accepts unencrypted connections and credentials/PII are sniffable and MITM-able on the wire.

server_certificate_validated.title: Server Certificate Validated
server_certificate_validated.description: Clients validate the server certificate AND hostname before sending credentials — PostgreSQL sslmode=verify-full (cert chains to a trusted CA and hostname matches), MySQL VERIFY_IDENTITY / REQUIRE X509. When false (sslmode=require/prefer/allow/disable or no CA pinning), the connection may be encrypted but the server is unauthenticated, leaving an active MITM able to intercept the session.

weak_tls_versions_enabled.title: Weak TLS Versions Enabled
weak_tls_versions_enabled.description: Interpreted boolean: the server negotiates a deprecated/weak TLS protocol version (TLS 1.0/1.1, SSLv3) or weak cipher suites for database connections. True means a downgrade-capable MITM or passive attacker can break the transport encryption. Modeled as an interpreted boolean rather than substring-matching the raw cipher/version directive to stay polarity-safe.

min_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version Accepted
min_tls_version.description: Lowest TLS protocol version the database server will accept for client connections (canonical shared-workspace attribute). A value of TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1/SSLv3 indicates a legacy floor exploitable by downgrade/known-cipher attacks; the secure floor is TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3. PG ssl_min_protocol_version, MySQL tls_version.

storage_encryption_enabled.title: At-Rest Storage Encryption Enabled
storage_encryption_enabled.description: Whether at-rest storage encryption is active for the data files, WAL/binlogs, automated backups and snapshots — RDS StorageEncrypted=true (AES-256 via KMS), TDE for Oracle/SQL Server, or an encrypted volume (LUKS) for self-managed engines. False means at-rest data is readable from disk/volume/snapshot theft; note RDS encryption is creation-time-only and is retrofitted only by encrypting a snapshot copy.

encrypted_at_rest.title: Data Encrypted at Rest
encrypted_at_rest.description: Canonical workspace flag asserting the store's data at rest is encrypted by some mechanism (TDE / RDS StorageEncrypted / encrypted volume). Used here as the AND-context for the customer-managed-key gap: when at-rest encryption is on but not backed by a customer-managed key, the second group fires. Reuses the canonical name across the workspace rather than a store-local synonym.

customer_managed_key_used.title: Customer-Managed Key Used
customer_managed_key_used.description: Whether the at-rest encryption is backed by a customer-managed KMS key (CMK) rather than the AWS-managed default key (or no distinct CMK). A customer-managed CMK gives independent key policy, scoped principal access, and revocation/rotation control. False — when encryption is otherwise enabled — leaves key custody and access policy outside the data owner's control.

db_credentials_in_secret_manager.title: DB Credentials in Secret Manager
db_credentials_in_secret_manager.description: Interpreted attestation: the database connection credentials are sourced at runtime from a secret manager / Vault rather than embedded in app config, environment files, or source. Secure value is true; fires on false, where the DB password lives in plaintext config/env and can be harvested from images, repos, or process memory and replayed for direct DB access.

dynamic_short_lived_db_credentials_used.title: Dynamic Short-Lived DB Credentials Used
dynamic_short_lived_db_credentials_used.description: Interpreted attestation: the application uses short-lived, automatically-issued dynamic DB credentials (e.g. HashiCorp Vault's database secrets engine issuing TTL'd creds) rather than a single long-lived shared static password. Secure value is true; fires on false, where a long-lived static password is used, so a single credential leak grants persistent direct DB access until manually rotated.

db_credentials_not_in_code_or_repo.title: DB Credentials Not in Code or Repo
db_credentials_not_in_code_or_repo.description: Interpreted attestation: no database connection string or password is hard-coded in application source code, committed config files, container images, or version-control history. Secure value is true; fires on false, where connection strings or DB passwords are committed to the repo or baked into images and harvested directly (MITRE T1552.001).

db_credentials_rotated_regularly.title: DB Credentials Rotated Regularly
db_credentials_rotated_regularly.description: Interpreted attestation: where static credentials cannot be fully eliminated, the DB password is rotated on a regular, enforced schedule (automated rotation policy) rather than left long-lived/unchanged. Secure value is true; fires on false, where a never-rotated static password remains valid indefinitely, maximizing the reuse window for a leaked credential.

backups_encrypted.title: Backups Encrypted
backups_encrypted.description: True when database backups/snapshots and dumps are encrypted at rest (RDS automated backups inherit StorageEncrypted=true with a KMS key; self-managed pg_dump/mysqldump output is encrypted). Insecure (false) when backups are written unencrypted — e.g. plaintext dumps in an open bucket — exposing the full dataset to theft of snapshots and enabling exfiltration from recovery copies.

point_in_time_recovery_enabled.title: Point-in-Time Recovery Enabled
point_in_time_recovery_enabled.description: True when point-in-time recovery / automated backups are enabled so the data store can be restored after destruction or ransomware — RDS BackupRetentionPeriod > 0, or equivalent WAL/binlog archiving with retention for self-managed engines. Insecure (false) when BackupRetentionPeriod=0 or no PITR/retention exists, so a compromised credential can destroy data with no recovery path.

backup_access_restricted.title: Backup Access Restricted
backup_access_restricted.description: True when access to the backup store (snapshot share permissions, backup bucket IAM/ACLs, snapshot copy/delete rights) is least-privilege and not world-readable/writable, so a compromised app/DB credential cannot read, copy, or delete recovery data. Insecure (false) when backups live in a world-readable bucket or the runtime credential holds delete/share rights over snapshots.

backup_immutability_enabled.title: Backup Immutability Enabled
backup_immutability_enabled.description: True when backups are immutable / integrity-protected (object-lock / WORM / append-only store, or vaulted snapshots that cannot be altered or deleted within retention), so an attacker who reaches the backup store cannot tamper with or delete recovery data (anti-forensics, ransomware). Insecure (false) when backups are mutable and deletable by the operating credential.

database_audit_logging_enabled.title: Database Audit Logging Enabled
database_audit_logging_enabled.description: True when database access/DML/DDL auditing is active (pgAudit loaded with object/role logging, MySQL audit log plugin, or RDS audit-log export). False means privileged and bulk-read activity goes unrecorded (defeats PCI DSS Req 10 / NIST AU family).

log_connections_enabled.title: Connection Logging Enabled
log_connections_enabled.description: True when connection logging is on (PostgreSQL log_connections=on / log_disconnections=on, or the MySQL equivalent) so login and session events are captured. False leaves authentication events unlogged, masking unauthorized access.

logs_stored_on_separate_system.title: Logs Stored on Separate System
logs_stored_on_separate_system.description: True when audit/database logs are shipped off-host to a centralized, append-only/immutable store with restricted access (CloudWatch export, SIEM forwarding) so a DB-account compromise cannot erase the local trail (PCI DSS Req 10, NIST AU-9). False means logs live only on the DB host and are deletable by the DB account.

log_retention_days.title: Log Retention (Days)
log_retention_days.description: Number of days audit/access logs are retained in the off-host store. Values below the regulatory minimum (PCI DSS Req 10 mandates ~1 year, here 365 days) leave insufficient forensic history to investigate and reconstruct a breach. Fires when retention is shorter than the required window.

unpatched_known_rce_cve.title: Unpatched Known RCE CVE
unpatched_known_rce_cve.description: True when the database engine runs an EoL major version or a minor behind a known-exploited CVE/CISA-KEV entry (e.g. CVE-2025-1094, the PostgreSQL libpq/psql invalid-UTF-8 SQL injection chaining to shell command execution; fixed in PG 17.3/16.7/15.11/14.16/13.19). True leaves a documented, weaponized exploitation path open with mandated KEV remediation timelines (CISA BOD 22-01).

data_residency_region_pinned.title: Data Residency Region Pinned
data_residency_region_pinned.description: True when the instance plus its read replicas, automated backups, and snapshot copies are confined to the approved residency region(s) and cannot drift cross-region. False means regulated PII may be stored or replicated outside the required jurisdiction (residency violation; NIST SP 800-122).
